liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Outstanding Good Lovin' with intricate lead work, syncopated rhythm and Pigpen in excellent form; The intro to Good Lovin' is described as crazy good [14][15]
- **How Long Blues** (1 review): How Long Blues is singled out as exceptional [12]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Vocal harmonies on Candyman, and later songs, are praised as impeccable [10]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Pigpen's piano playing on Truckin' is especially loved [9]
- **Cocaine Blues** (1 review): Heard as Jerry's nod to Mississippi John Hurt, with a similar light-hearted yet deep blues feel [13]
- **Wake Up Little Susie** (1 review): Wake Up Little Susie and Swing Low Sweet Chariot are singled out as favorites in the acoustic set [15]
- **Easy Wind** (1 review): Described as a classic version of Easy Wind [4]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Singled out as a great version of I Know You Rider [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **How Long Blues**: rare: 5 archived performances [16]
- **Cocaine Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **Wake Up Little Susie**: rare: 9 archived performances [16]
- **Swing Low Sweet Chariot**: rare: 13 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-08-19.aud.taback.cdjones.81775.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 153 min; rated 4/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer has heard worse recordings; the acoustic set is very nice; The recording's flaws give it a vintage tone that suits the show; Recording has some rough edges but is worth downloading [9][12][14]
- **gd1970-08-19.aud.taback.minches.81605.flac16**: audience recording; 26 songs; 128 min; rated 3.67/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is middling, neither the best nor worst, but the acoustic set is wonderful; Tape deck was paused between songs, causing whooshing noise, partly edited out, and the first notes of many songs are missing [2][8]
- **gd70-08-19.aud.cotsman.11797.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 141 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording captures the electric set loudly and clearly but handles the acoustic portion poorly; The acoustic set is slightly chopped up, though fidelity is otherwise fairly good; This audience master is missing several songs, per the info file, and its quality is said to be misrepresented by the Taper's Compendium [3][4][5]

## Around the show

- The August 1970 run drew considerable press, including a Rolling Stone article on the band's changing sound [5]
- The acoustic set features fine vocals and Workingman's Dead and American Beauty material [14]
- Nothing here matches the previous night's Man's World, but the electric set is overall hotter [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-08-19.aud.taback.cdjones.81775.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by CD Jones; source: Set 1: AUD>MC>D>FLAC>AIFF>FLAC Set 2: AUD>MC>R>PCM>D>CD>EAC>SHN>AIFF>FLAC [1]. Also: Original tapers stopped the tape between most acoustic songs and some electric ones; the uploader crossfaded tracks to smooth the cuts; Uploader decoded sources with xACT, lightly edited in Peak LE 5.2, crossfaded in Jam 5, and encoded to FLAC with Toast [1]
- **gd1970-08-19.aud.taback.minches.81605.flac16**: taped by Gene Taback; transferred by David Minches; source: Master Audience Cassette; Sony TC-124 with Sony Stereo Mic [2]. Also: Transferred from cassettes provided by Gene [2]
- **gd70-08-19.aud.cotsman.11797.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke, Matt Vernon, JCotsman; source: Audience [3]
